newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end bourse trade with modest gains.
newsitem.headline: German shares end bourse trade with modest gains.

text.p: German shares shrugged off an early bout of profit-taking to end bourse trade on Thursday slightly higher, boosted by gains in the banking sector and continuing a rally begun on Tuesday.
Dealers said the DAX index of 30 leading shares was still aiming for the technical and psychological level of 2,800 points and said it could reach that level this week.
The blue-chip DAX index touched an all-time bourse high of 2,785.16 points in early dealings, then pared gains.
The DAX index ended bourse trade up 3.58 points at 2,777.01 points and was mostly steady at 2,777.48 in post-bourse IBIS electronic trading.
German government bond strength and another record close on Wall Street were also supporting the market, dealers said.

The day's main action was in the banking sector, with over three million Deutsche Bank AG shares and almost three million Commerzbank AG shares changing hands in computer trade. Over a million Commerzbank shares were also traded in bourse dealings.
Commerzbank jumped to a new year high of 37.38 marks in IBIS trade and was up almost four percent or 1.40 marks at 36.65 marks in bourse dealings.
Commerzbank shares ended the bourse session up 1.35 marks at 36.65 marks.

Traders said the whole banking sector was boosted by talk of mergers, which have been rife in the sector since July when Deutsche Bank AG said it had amassed a 5.21 percent stake in Munich-based rival Bayerische Vereinsbank AG.

But Commerzbank moved to quash merger speculation, saying it saw no one single large investor buying up the group's shares and said the strong rise in its share price was largely due to the fact that the shares were earlier undervalued.

Outside of the banking sector, shares in national airline Lufthansa AG were amongst the major movers, ending down 30 pfennigs at 20.25 marks after Bonn said it would plan to sell the rest of its 36 percent stake in Lufthansa.
